quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Reference: Missing Antecedent
quests.faultySentence: Ana wants to become a veterinarian because she loves them.
quests.incorrectPart: she loves them
quests.correctedSentence: Ana wants to become a veterinarian because she loves animals.
quests.correctedPart: she loves animals
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Them' has nothing to point back to; the only earlier noun is the singular 'a veterinarian'. Naming what she loves, 'animals', supplies the missing reference.
quests.nativeTip: Look for the noun that 'them' should refer back to — is any plural noun mentioned earlier in the sentence?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Reference: Substitute Word Without a Matching Noun
quests.faultySentence: Omar is studying architecture because his grandfather was one.
quests.incorrectPart: was one
quests.correctedSentence: Omar is studying architecture because his grandfather was an architect.
quests.correctedPart: was an architect
quests.ruleExplanation: 'One' would have to replace 'an architect', but the sentence only mentions 'architecture', the subject area. Naming the profession directly closes the gap.
quests.nativeTip: 'One' stands in for a noun that has already been named — has the sentence named a type of person, or only a field of study?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Reference: Empty It After a Prepositional Phrase
quests.faultySentence: In the survey, it showed that most users prefer dark mode.
quests.incorrectPart: In the survey, it showed
quests.correctedSentence: The survey showed that most users prefer dark mode.
quests.correctedPart: The survey showed
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It' has no noun to point to, because 'the survey' sits inside a prepositional phrase. Making the survey the subject removes the empty pronoun.
quests.nativeTip: What does 'it' refer to here? Is there a noun before it that could be the one doing the showing?

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Modifiers: Prepositional Phrase Near Its Target
quests.faultySentence: The waiter served pasta to the couple with garlic bread.
quests.incorrectPart: pasta to the couple with garlic bread
quests.correctedSentence: The waiter served the couple pasta with garlic bread.
quests.correctedPart: the couple pasta with garlic bread
quests.ruleExplanation: Placed after 'the couple', 'with garlic bread' seems to describe the diners. It belongs with the pasta, so the phrase must follow 'pasta' directly.
quests.nativeTip: Ask who or what has the garlic bread — the couple, or the pasta? A phrase should sit next to the noun it describes.

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Modifiers: Prepositional Phrase Near Its Target
quests.faultySentence: I bought a used car from a dealer with a broken air conditioner, so I negotiated a lower price.
quests.incorrectPart: a used car from a dealer with a broken air conditioner
quests.correctedSentence: I bought a used car with a broken air conditioner from a dealer, so I negotiated a lower price.
quests.correctedPart: a used car with a broken air conditioner from a dealer
quests.ruleExplanation: Cars have air conditioners and dealers do not, so 'with a broken air conditioner' should sit right after 'car' to describe the vehicle.
quests.nativeTip: The buyer negotiated a lower price — which item has the broken air conditioner, the dealer or the car?

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Modifiers: Prepositional Phrase Near Its Target
quests.faultySentence: The auditor reviewed the invoices for the client with several errors and flagged each one for correction.
quests.incorrectPart: the invoices for the client with several errors
quests.correctedSentence: The auditor reviewed the invoices with several errors for the client and flagged each one for correction.
quests.correctedPart: the invoices with several errors for the client
quests.ruleExplanation: 'With several errors' sits next to 'the client', so it seems to describe the client. Moving it directly after 'invoices' ties the errors to the documents that contain them.
quests.nativeTip: Which has the errors — the invoices or the client? Place the phrase beside the noun it describes.

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Modifiers: Infinitive of Purpose
quests.faultySentence: To improve customer satisfaction, the survey was redesigned by the team.
quests.incorrectPart: the survey was redesigned by the team
quests.correctedSentence: To improve customer satisfaction, the team redesigned the survey.
quests.correctedPart: the team redesigned the survey
quests.ruleExplanation: An opening 'to' phrase names a goal, and the subject that follows should be the one pursuing it. A survey cannot pursue a goal, so making 'the team' the subject fixes the link.
quests.nativeTip: Who is 'to improve customer satisfaction' meant to describe? The subject right after the comma should be the one with that goal.

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Modifiers: Introductory Prepositional Phrase
quests.faultySentence: At the age of ten, her family moved to Toronto.
quests.incorrectPart: At the age of ten, her family moved
quests.correctedSentence: When she was ten, her family moved to Toronto.
quests.correctedPart: When she was ten, her family moved
quests.ruleExplanation: 'At the age of ten' attaches to the subject that follows, 'her family', which cannot be ten years old. Turning the phrase into a clause with its own subject, 'When she was ten', fixes it.
quests.nativeTip: Whose age is 'ten'? The phrase needs a subject that could actually be ten years old.

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Modifiers: Introductory Adjective Phrase
quests.faultySentence: Tired after the long flight, the hotel check-in line seemed endless.
quests.incorrectPart: the hotel check-in line seemed endless
quests.correctedSentence: Tired after the long flight, the travelers found the hotel check-in line endless.
quests.correctedPart: the travelers found the hotel check-in line endless
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Tired' describes people, but the subject is 'the hotel check-in line'. Naming the travelers as the subject gives the opening phrase something logical to describe.
quests.nativeTip: Who is tired after the flight? The word right after the comma should name that person.

quests.conceptTitle: Negation Scope: Not All vs All ... Not
quests.faultySentence: All the applicants were not accepted; three received job offers.
quests.incorrectPart: All the applicants were not accepted
quests.correctedSentence: Not all the applicants were accepted; three received job offers.
quests.correctedPart: Not all the applicants were accepted
quests.ruleExplanation: 'All ... were not accepted' can suggest nobody was accepted. Since three did receive offers, the intended meaning is 'not all', which places 'not' at the start so it limits 'all' rather than the verb.
quests.nativeTip: The second part says three received offers. Does the first part mean nobody was accepted, or that only some people were?

quests.conceptTitle: Negation Scope: Not Everyone vs Everyone ... Not
quests.faultySentence: Everyone can't attend the workshop on Friday, so we scheduled a second session.
quests.incorrectPart: Everyone can't attend
quests.correctedSentence: Not everyone can attend the workshop on Friday, so we scheduled a second session.
quests.correctedPart: Not everyone can attend
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone can't' is easily read as 'no one can', but the second session shows only some people are unavailable. 'Not everyone can attend' says exactly that.
quests.nativeTip: A second session was added. Does that suggest nobody can come, or that some people cannot?

quests.conceptTitle: Negation Scope: Not Both vs Both ... Not
quests.faultySentence: Both of the suppliers didn't meet the deadline; one of them delivered two days early.
quests.incorrectPart: Both of the suppliers didn't meet the deadline
quests.correctedSentence: Not both of the suppliers met the deadline; one of them delivered two days early.
quests.correctedPart: Not both of the suppliers met the deadline
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Both ... didn't' can mean 'neither did', which clashes with the supplier that delivered early. 'Not both met the deadline' correctly says only one of them missed it.
quests.nativeTip: One supplier delivered early. Does the first clause mean neither made the deadline, or that only one of them missed it?

quests.conceptTitle: Introductory Comparisons: Comparing Like Elements
quests.faultySentence: Unlike her older brother, Nora's grades have always been excellent.
quests.incorrectPart: Nora's grades have always been excellent
quests.correctedSentence: Unlike her older brother, Nora has always earned excellent grades.
quests.correctedPart: Nora has always earned excellent grades
quests.ruleExplanation: The opening phrase sets a person, her brother, against 'Nora's grades', which is a mismatch. Making Nora the subject compares person with person.
quests.nativeTip: 'Unlike her older brother' compares two people. Does the rest of the sentence give you a person to set against him?

quests.conceptTitle: Introductory Comparisons: Comparing Like Elements
quests.faultySentence: In contrast to last year's budget, the marketing department received less funding this year.
quests.incorrectPart: the marketing department received less funding this year
quests.correctedSentence: In contrast to last year's budget, this year's budget gives the marketing department less funding.
quests.correctedPart: this year's budget gives the marketing department less funding
quests.ruleExplanation: A budget is being contrasted with a department, which is not a fair comparison. Making 'this year's budget' the subject compares budget with budget.
quests.nativeTip: The opening phrase contrasts two budgets. What should the main clause be about so the two items match?

quests.conceptTitle: Introductory Comparisons: Comparing Like Elements
quests.faultySentence: Compared to the previous version, the new app's speed has improved dramatically.
quests.incorrectPart: the new app's speed has improved dramatically
quests.correctedSentence: Compared to the previous version, the new app runs dramatically faster.
quests.correctedPart: the new app runs dramatically faster
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence compares the previous version with the app's speed. Using the app itself as the subject, 'the new app runs dramatically faster', keeps like with like.
quests.nativeTip: The opening phrase compares versions of software. What should the subject be so the comparison stays version-to-version?

quests.conceptTitle: Noun Reference: Former and Latter
quests.faultySentence: Marta wrote the proposal and Diego edited it, so the latter deserves credit for the original ideas.
quests.incorrectPart: the latter deserves
quests.correctedSentence: Marta wrote the proposal and Diego edited it, so the former deserves credit for the original ideas.
quests.correctedPart: the former deserves
quests.ruleExplanation: Marta, the writer, is named first, so she is 'the former'; Diego, the editor, is 'the latter'. Original ideas come from the writer, so the sentence needs 'the former'.
quests.nativeTip: 'The former' means the first person named and 'the latter' the second. Who came up with the original ideas, the writer or the editor?

quests.conceptTitle: Noun Reference: Former and Latter
quests.faultySentence: Of the two options, cycling and driving, the latter is healthier and produces no emissions.
quests.incorrectPart: the latter is healthier
quests.correctedSentence: Of the two options, cycling and driving, the former is healthier and produces no emissions.
quests.correctedPart: the former is healthier
quests.ruleExplanation: Cycling is listed first, so it is 'the former'. Cycling, not driving, is the healthier, emission-free choice, so 'the latter' points to the wrong option.
quests.nativeTip: Match 'former' and 'latter' to the order the options were listed. Which option is healthier and emission-free?

quests.conceptTitle: Noun Reference: Respectively Matches in Order
quests.faultySentence: Priya and Jonas work as a pilot and a chef at a restaurant and an airline, respectively.
quests.incorrectPart: at a restaurant and an airline, respectively
quests.correctedSentence: Priya and Jonas work as a pilot and a chef at an airline and a restaurant, respectively.
quests.correctedPart: at an airline and a restaurant, respectively
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Respectively' pairs the first item with the first item: pilot with the first workplace, chef with the second. A pilot works at an airline, so the workplaces must be listed in that order.
quests.nativeTip: 'Respectively' matches items in order. Which workplace goes with a pilot, and which with a chef?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Consistency: Avoiding Shifts in Person
quests.faultySentence: If a customer is dissatisfied, you should be offered a refund.
quests.incorrectPart: you should be offered
quests.correctedSentence: If a customer is dissatisfied, they should be offered a refund.
quests.correctedPart: they should be offered
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence begins with a third-person subject, 'a customer', then switches to 'you'. Keeping the reference consistent requires 'they' (or 'the customer').
quests.nativeTip: The sentence starts by talking about 'a customer'. Which pronoun keeps referring to that same person?

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Consistency: Avoiding Shifts in Person
quests.faultySentence: Students often perform better when they sleep well, and we also concentrate more in class.
quests.incorrectPart: and we also concentrate
quests.correctedSentence: Students often perform better when they sleep well, and they also concentrate more in class.
quests.correctedPart: and they also concentrate
quests.ruleExplanation: The first half is about 'students' ('they'), but the second half jumps to 'we'. Staying with 'they' keeps the reference on the same group.
quests.nativeTip: Who is the whole sentence about? Check that both halves point to the same group.

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Consistency: Avoiding Shifts in Person
quests.faultySentence: When one travels abroad, you should carry a copy of your passport.
quests.incorrectPart: When one travels abroad
quests.correctedSentence: When you travel abroad, you should carry a copy of your passport.
quests.correctedPart: When you travel abroad
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence begins with the impersonal 'one' but continues with 'you' and 'your'. Using 'you' from the start keeps the address consistent.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the pronouns later in the sentence ('you', 'your'). Which subject would match them?

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Participial Phrases: Placing the Phrase Near the Doer
quests.faultySentence: The technician photographed the cracked wall standing on a ladder.
quests.incorrectPart: The technician photographed the cracked wall standing on a ladder
quests.correctedSentence: Standing on a ladder, the technician photographed the cracked wall.
quests.correctedPart: Standing on a ladder, the technician photographed the cracked wall
quests.ruleExplanation: Placed after 'wall', 'standing on a ladder' seems to describe the wall. Putting it at the front, right before 'the technician', ties it to the person doing the standing.
quests.nativeTip: Who is standing on the ladder, the technician or the wall? The phrase should sit next to that person.

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Participial Phrases: Placing the Phrase Near the Doer
quests.faultySentence: We noticed a strange smell entering the kitchen.
quests.incorrectPart: We noticed a strange smell entering the kitchen
quests.correctedSentence: Entering the kitchen, we noticed a strange smell.
quests.correctedPart: Entering the kitchen, we noticed a strange smell
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Entering the kitchen' follows 'smell', so it sounds as if the smell entered. Opening with the phrase and then naming 'we' shows who actually entered.
quests.nativeTip: What was entering the kitchen, the smell or the people? Put the phrase beside the one who was entering.

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Participial Phrases: Placing the Phrase Near the Doer
quests.faultySentence: The nurse handed the patient a glass of water shaking with fever.
quests.incorrectPart: the patient a glass of water shaking with fever
quests.correctedSentence: The nurse handed the patient, shaking with fever, a glass of water.
quests.correctedPart: the patient, shaking with fever, a glass of water
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'water', 'shaking with fever' seems to describe the glass. It belongs beside 'the patient', the person who is ill.
quests.nativeTip: Who is shaking with fever, the patient or the water? The phrase should stay beside the noun it describes.

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Reference: Missing Antecedent
quests.faultySentence: According to the handbook, they require all visitors to sign in at reception.
quests.incorrectPart: they require all visitors to sign in
quests.correctedSentence: According to the handbook, all visitors are required to sign in at reception.
quests.correctedPart: all visitors are required to sign in
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They' has no antecedent; the only noun is 'the handbook', which is singular. Stating the requirement directly removes the unexplained pronoun.
quests.nativeTip: Who is 'they'? Is any group named earlier that could be the one requiring this?

quests.conceptTitle: Relative Clause Attachment: Clause Beside Its Noun
quests.faultySentence: The department restructured its reporting system after the audit, which had been outdated for years.
quests.incorrectPart: its reporting system after the audit, which had been outdated for years
quests.correctedSentence: The department restructured its reporting system, which had been outdated for years, after the audit.
quests.correctedPart: its reporting system, which had been outdated for years, after the audit
quests.ruleExplanation: Because 'which' follows 'the audit', it seems to describe the audit. Moving the clause directly after 'reporting system' shows it is the system that was outdated.
quests.nativeTip: What had been outdated, the audit or the system? Keep the 'which' clause right beside its noun.

quests.conceptTitle: Pronoun Reference: Ambiguous Possessive
quests.faultySentence: Ravi told Omar his laptop was broken, so Ravi lent him a spare one.
quests.incorrectPart: Ravi told Omar his laptop was broken
quests.correctedSentence: Ravi told Omar that Omar's laptop was broken, so Ravi lent him a spare one.
quests.correctedPart: Ravi told Omar that Omar's laptop was broken
quests.ruleExplanation: 'His' could point to Ravi or Omar. Since Ravi lends Omar a spare, it is Omar's laptop that is broken, and naming him removes the doubt.
quests.nativeTip: Whose laptop is broken? Use the second half of the sentence to decide, then make that owner clear.

quests.conceptTitle: Dangling Modifiers: Gerund Phrase
quests.faultySentence: By analyzing customer complaints, several product flaws were identified.
quests.incorrectPart: several product flaws were identified
quests.correctedSentence: By analyzing customer complaints, the team identified several product flaws.
quests.correctedPart: the team identified several product flaws
quests.ruleExplanation: 'By analyzing' needs a doer, but the subject is 'several product flaws', which cannot analyze anything. Naming 'the team' as the subject supplies one.
quests.nativeTip: Who is analyzing the complaints? The subject after the comma should be the analyzer.

quests.conceptTitle: Misplaced Modifiers: Participial Phrase Near Its Noun
quests.faultySentence: They sell handmade candles to tourists made from local beeswax.
quests.incorrectPart: candles to tourists made from local beeswax
quests.correctedSentence: They sell handmade candles made from local beeswax to tourists.
quests.correctedPart: candles made from local beeswax to tourists
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Made from local beeswax' follows 'tourists', so it seems to describe them. It belongs right after 'candles'.
quests.nativeTip: What is made from beeswax, the candles or the tourists? Keep the phrase beside its noun.

quests.conceptTitle: Sentence Clarity: Serial Comma Prevents Misreading
quests.faultySentence: We thanked our parents, Maria and Tom, four people who helped organize the party.
quests.incorrectPart: our parents, Maria and Tom
quests.correctedSentence: We thanked our parents, Maria, and Tom, four people who helped organize the party.
quests.correctedPart: our parents, Maria, and Tom
quests.ruleExplanation: Without a comma before 'and', 'Maria and Tom' can read as a description of 'our parents', which would give only two people. Adding the comma separates all four: two parents, Maria, and Tom.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence says four people helped. Count how many people the list currently seems to name.
